title: People v. Sanchez
summary: Former Mayor Antonio Sanchez was convicted of rape with homicide for the deaths of Eileen Sarmenta and Allan Gomez. The Supreme Court affirmed the death penalty, ruling that the crime was attended by the aggravating circumstances of abuse of authority and use of a motor vehicle.
doctrine: When rape is committed and homicide results by reason or on the occasion thereof, the crime is the special complex crime of rape with homicide punishable by death. The use of position of authority to facilitate the commission of the crime is an aggravating circumstance.
fullText:
PER CURIAM:

This is an automatic review of the death sentence imposed on Mayor Antonio L. Sanchez for the crime of rape with homicide.

The evidence established that on June 28, 1993, the victims Eileen Sarmenta and Allan Gomez were abducted and brought to the Pasig River resort owned by Mayor Sanchez. Sarmenta was raped by the accused and his co-accused. Thereafter, both victims were killed.

The special complex crime of rape with homicide is punishable by death under Article 335 of the Revised Penal Code. The accused took advantage of his position as mayor to facilitate the commission of the crime.
